dct_description_sm:
The WRS mapping provides the base data to characterize the location of important surface and groundwater features and areas in the Credit River Watershed. The mapped components of the WRS include the following layers:

  1. Watercourses (2026) Click for Metadata here: CVC WRS Watercourses (2026) Metadata
  2. Waterbodies (2026) Click for Metadata here: CVC WRS Waterbodies (2026) Metadata
  3. Wetlands (2025) Click for Metadata here: CVC WRS Wetlands (2025) Metadata
  4. Seepage areas and springs (1996-2024) Click for Metadata here: CVC WRS Seepage areas and springs (1996-2024) Metadata
  5. Highly Vulnerable Aquifers (HVAs) (2024) Click for Metadata here: CVC WRS Highly Vulnerable Aquifers (HVAs) (2024) Metadata
  6. Significant Groundwater Recharge Areas (SGRAs) (2024) Click for Metadata here: CVC WRS Significant Groundwater Recharge Areas (SGRAs) (2024) Metadata
  7. Candidate Ecologically Significant Groundwater Recharge Areas (ESGRAs) (2022) Click for Metadata here: CVC WRS Candidate Ecologically Significant Groundwater Recharge Areas (ESGRAs) (2022) Metadata
  8. Watercourses with high simulated groundwater discharge (2026) Click for Metadata here: CVC WRS Watercourses with high simulated groundwater discharge (2026) Metadata
  9. Potential groundwater recharge areas (2022). This dataset is created and managed by the Oak Ridges Moraine Ground Water Program. To request this mapping, please contact the ORMGP by visiting their webpage (Oak Ridges Moraine Groundwater Program | Ontario). 

Please scroll down to view the available layers. Click on the layer(s) you're interested in to download the data.

NOTE: This dataset cannot be downloaded directly from ArcGIS Online; please use the CVC's Open Data portal to download the data.

For more information, see CVC Water Resource System Mapping User Guide (2026)
